sections.h2: Offices that handle your tax bill
sections.html:
Two offices in the county government building on South Prairie Street in Bloomfield deal with a property tax bill. The Assessor lists and values property. The Collector of Revenue mails the bills and takes the money.

Stoddard County tax offices in Bloomfield
OfficeAddressPhone
Collector of Revenue401 S. Prairie St, P.O. Box 80, Bloomfield, MO 63825(573) 568-3327
Assessor401 South Prairie, P.O. Box 307, Bloomfield, MO 63825(573) 568-3163

The Collector is staffed weekdays from half past eight until half past four and is shut on state and federal holidays. The Assessor's website offers real estate and personal property lookups by account number, name or address.

Stoddard County fills the southeast corner of Missouri. Bloomfield is the seat and Dexter the largest city. About 28,284 people live in 13,409 homes, and owners occupy 71.8% of them. The median owner-reported home value is $143,300, median rent is $760 and median household income is $57,957. Seven public districts reach into the county: Advance R-IV, Bell City R-II, Bernie R-XIII, Bloomfield R-XIV, Dexter R-XI, Puxico R-VIII and Richland R-I.

Collection opens November 1 and ends December 31. The County Clerk delivers the tax books in the fall, the bills are printed after that, and they reach mailboxes in November.

Once December 31 is behind you, added charges hit on the first of every month, in the amounts printed on the statement. A mailed check needs a U.S. Postal Service postmark dated within the month, since a payment that falls short of the added penalties is sent back. If the bill never reached you, the penalty still applies.

The Collector's website looks up a bill by owner name, parcel number, property address or account number, and shows payment history. You can pay with cash at the counter, a personal check, a money order or a cashier's check, or by card on the website or by phone, where a convenience fee applies. The drop box by the entrance to the government building is open around the clock, but a late check left there without the penalty comes back to you. Tax paid out of a mortgage escrow account will not appear in the online database.

Yes, a plan exists for the real estate bill. The county has run it since the 2010 tax year. It starts from last year's real estate payment, divides it by eleven, and collects ten equal pieces, then the actual balance as the eleventh. Money leaves a checking or savings account automatically, on the 5th or the 20th.

  • You cannot join while any real estate tax is past due.
  • A parcel whose tax runs through a mortgage escrow is not eligible.
  • A missed withdrawal can end the plan, and any amount left unpaid at year end draws the usual penalties.

A county resident who is 62 or older on January 1, owns the home and lives in it can lock in the real estate tax on that home. The credit does not exempt you from tax. You still pay a bill, just a frozen one.

First-time filers have from January 1 to June 30. Renewal paperwork is mailed beginning February 1 and is also due June 30. A notary must witness the first application, and the license or state ID has to show the home address. The homestead covers a primary residence on up to five acres, which leaves out barns, commercial ground and farmland.

New construction and additions are addressed too. Before you list, ask the Collector at (573) 568-3327 how a sale or a remodel would affect your frozen base year.

sections.h2: If your assessed value looks too high
sections.html:
Call the Assessor at (573) 568-3163 and ask for this year's Board of Equalization filing date. At the board, RSMo 138.060 removes any presumption that the assessor is right. In a county of this type the assessor must carry the burden of proof when a parcel's assessed value climbed 15% or more from the prior assessment, unless new construction or improvement explains the jump.

Paying while you contest follows RSMo 139.031. The whole bill is due before delinquency, along with a written statement of your grounds delivered to the Collector. A circuit court suit for recovery has to begin within 90 days of that protest.

RSMo 140.150 allows land with unpaid tax to be offered for sale on the fourth Monday in August. Before that, the collector mails a letter to the record owner. When the assessed value is above $1,000, a second letter goes out by certified mail. Notices of delinquent tax certificate sales appear on the Collector's website.

At closing, the working rule is that taxes ride with the land, not the owner. The statement is passed to the buyer, and buyer and seller agree who pays what when the bill comes due. Buyers are expected to learn the tax status before they buy, so a title company will probably ask for a payoff or a proration. Missouri's Form MO-PTC is a separate state refund claim for some seniors, disabled owners and renters, and the Department of Revenue decides who qualifies.

Stoddard County is mostly rural, and its small offices are used to handling closings by phone and mail. A seller who lives out of town can order the payoff by phone, mail a check to P.O. Box 80 or pay by card on the website, so there is little reason to wait until the last week to deal with the bill. Keep the receipt or a printout of your payment history for the closing file.

Here is the order that usually works for a Stoddard County seller. First, look up your bill on the Collector's website by owner name, parcel number or address, and confirm what is owed. Second, call (573) 568-3327 if anything looks wrong or if you are on the installment plan. Third, give the title company the payoff or proration figure so it can appear on the settlement statement. Fourth, check whether a senior homestead credit is in place, because the buyer will want to know how it affects the first bill after the sale.

If you owe tax when you decide to sell, call the Collector first for a payoff figure and make sure the installment plan, if you use one, is settled or current. Any unpaid balance comes out of your proceeds at the table. A cash buyer can close without waiting for a lender, which helps when you want the tax cleared before the August sale list, but compare the offer with what a listing would leave after fees and repairs.

faqs.q: Where is Stoddard County property tax paid?
faqs.a: At the Collector of Revenue, 401 S. Prairie St in Bloomfield, by mail to P.O. Box 80, Bloomfield, MO 63825, or online through the Collector's website.

faqs.q: What is the last day to pay without penalty?
faqs.a: December 31. Collection begins November 1, and extra charges start accruing on the first of each month after the deadline.

faqs.q: Is there a way to spread the bill over the year?
faqs.a: Yes, for real estate tax only. Ten equal monthly withdrawals are followed by a final payment of the balance. Past-due accounts and escrowed parcels cannot join.

faqs.q: Which party pays the tax at a sale?
faqs.a: Buyer and seller decide that at closing. The statement should go to the buyer, and taxes stay with the property.

faqs.q: What age qualifies for the homestead freeze?
faqs.a: Sixty-two on January 1, plus ownership and primary residence of the home. New applications are accepted from January 1 through June 30.
